ac8353ac91: The hardest part of writing a song
4d097ad963:
Writing a song isn't hard. What's hard is building sharp powers of observation in daily life,
and training yourself to record things faster and more efficiently.
Hardest of all is carrying that feeling, that moment of being moved,
across whole into the listener's ears, and even their heart.
1167f48b0b: 〈月亮代表我的心〉 and 〈綠島小夜曲〉 are still sung today for a simple reason: every listener finds themselves in the song.
0f6741f3b9: News, conversations, travel, a lovely melody: all of these are inputs. Once information enters your mind and gets sorted, out come the words and melodies we want.
ce555d1ba7: The keywords of an article are enough to build a "word source"; its main point carries enough weight to hold up a strong hook. Together they form a song's source and its signature.
79ef382b63: Imitate the songwriters you love, find your direction in their work, then develop a style of your own. A melody someone has used before, once reworked, can become another song.

43dbc3c811: Kuo Ying-nan's Amis songs, ChthoniC's Taiwanese folk elements: art that once belonged to a niche later reached the world stage and became sounds everyone knows.

88d60d0590: Pop songs have no rules; just write whatever comes
96c5d77caf: MythPop songs have set forms and formulas. Grasp the big principles and your writing has direction.
ddbbfe14f3: People who don't play an instrument can't write good songs
2b9746218b: MythHumming, recording and writing words down are all songwriting. An instrument helps, but it's no entry requirement.
4f014a762a: You have to have lyrics before you can write music
9a57930dd6: MythThere's no rule about words or music first; writing the melody and then the lyrics is very common.
6faf6f733c: FactAnalyse the work you love, imitate its techniques, then develop a style of your own.
456438aac1: You can copy someone else's lyrics word for word
6a37f26479: MythYou imitate the techniques and structure; copying word for word is infringement, and it loses the point of writing.
4c7bc987e2: Pop music reflects its era, and it's an art of conversation
a29f199ec0: FactA song talks to its listeners and records what its era looked like.
